claims.text: The as-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous fcc matrix.
The elements are evenly distributed in the as-manufactured alloy.
Under oxidizing conditions, aluminum and chromium selectively oxidize.
Selective oxidation produces a continuous and adherent scale consisting primarily of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The Al2O3- and Cr2O3-rich scale retards further degradation of the fcc matrix by limiting oxygen ingress.
Reducing conditions produce limited, discontinuous, or unstable oxide coverage.
The absence or instability of a protective scale under reducing conditions permits deeper oxygen diffusion and internal oxidation.
Internal oxidation under reducing conditions leads to microstructural degradation.
Oxidizing exposure at 750–850 °C will produce a thin, uniform, and well-adhered oxide layer.
The oxide formed under oxidizing exposure will significantly slow degradation and preserve the integrity of the fcc matrix.
Reducing exposure will accelerate internal oxidation relative to oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will cause early microstructural changes such as subsurface voids or phase degradation.
The unexposed as-manufactured alloy has minimal pre-existing oxidation.
Bulk heating at 750–850 °C does not induce phase transformations in this alloy.
Controlled cooling rates can prevent thermal shock or oxide-scale spallation under the proposed conditions.
Protective-scale formation is expected to dominate the alloy's degradation behavior.
Synergistic elemental interactions under cyclic thermal stress may alter oxide-scale stability.
